rationale: The two source notes about deciding without a local StopSign and about late Promises are accurate as behavior, but a quorum-intersection check shows they cannot by themselves explain the run-13 trace. With five nodes and three-node quorums, an accept quorum at index 38 and the leader's prepare quorum must intersect, so any leader that gets 38 chosen has either merged a promise carrying the StopSign or accepted the StopSign itself before deciding it. The trace only establishes that leader 4 had no StopSign when it sent node 3's AcceptSync. This update restates the interpretation with that upstream phase marked unresolved and softens the two knowledge uses so they are recorded as source-consistent alternatives rather than the established cause.

knowledge.assertion: A source-consistent way for a leader to hold a prepare quorum without a StopSign another node has accepted: a Promise arriving after the quorum contributes no log_sync. It is not established for run 13, because a late-promising accept-quorum member still has to intersect the prepare quorum and the receipt does not show which promises leader 4 received.

Explains how a decided index of 38 can exist on a leader whose own accepted index is lower only if is_chosen counted follower-reported indices; the receipt does not show whether leader 4 itself held the StopSign when it decided 38, so this remains a source-level possibility rather than the observed cause.

interpretations.rationale: The executed trace shows the stall and its downstream mechanism. Receipt c0f9c7117f564fd7a8b74b629988f177 ran randomized_reconfig_diagnose_lag (exit 0, test passed); its declared comparison (converged_all true, gated on progressed and reconfigured) is complete and violated on event 1, which reports decided 38,38,37,38,38 after 150 fair-delivery rounds, well past the 100-tick resend timeout. The same event records node 3 at accepted 37, decided 37, leader pid 4, promise ballot n=2, zero PrepareReq and one Promise sent, with the inbound trace prepare:0-0>0-0|prepare:0-0>0-0|prepare:0-0>0-0|promise:0-0>0-0|promise:0-0>0-0|promise:0-0>0-0|accsync1:0-0>37-0|decide2:37-0>37-37|decide3:37-37>37-37. The AcceptSync with sequence counter 1 raised node 3 from 0 to accepted 37 and left decided at 0, so it carried no StopSign: create_log_sync always attaches the leader's local StopSign, which means leader 4 had none when it sent that sync. The two later Decides carry sequence counters 2 and 3, the immediate successors of that AcceptSync's counter, so check_msg_status returns Expected for both and handle_decide runs update_decided_idx_and_get_accepted_idx; the first sets decided to min(carried decided index, flushed accepted index) = 37 and the second leaves it at 37. Node 3 never sends a PrepareReq, so no reconnection and no AcceptSync follow. Because the periodic resends reuse the leader's last used sequence number for node 3, which node 3 has already consumed, further Decide or AcceptStopSign resends are Outdated and are ignored; the missing StopSign is therefore never delivered. How leader 4 came to decide 38 while its sync to node 3 lacked the StopSign is not established by this receipt: with five nodes and three-node quorums the prepare and accept quorums intersect, so the leader must have merged a StopSign-bearing Promise or accepted the StopSign itself after sending that sync. Either way the consequence for node 3 is the same and is what the ticket records: a decided index it cannot accept, with a clamping Decide path and no sequence gap to trigger recovery. Agreement is unaffected because no two nodes reported different values at any decided index.
counterevidence: A missing AcceptStopSign does not always stall: in the constructed clean-miss run the periodic Decide was sequence-ahead and the follower reconnected, after which an AcceptSync repaired it.
A leadership change, or an external reconnected() call, leads to Prepare/Promise/AcceptSync, and create_log_sync attaches the leader's current StopSign, so those events repair the follower.
Agreement is unaffected: divergences stayed 0 and no node reported a different value at a decided index, so this is a progress/availability defect for one follower.
If the leader accepted the StopSign before sending the AcceptSync to node 3, that sync would have carried it and no gap would have formed.
limitations: One seeded schedule and one lagging follower; the trace records only the first twelve Paxos messages delivered to node 3 after the lossy phase, so later traffic and node 3's lossy-phase history are not shown.

The receipt does not record which promise or forwarded StopSign gave leader 4 the StopSign, when it accepted it, or the log_sync content of the AcceptSync, so the upstream order is inferred from the accepted indices, the trace and the source paths.
Five nodes, MemoryStorage, unit batch, no snapshots and no next configuration started; flexible quorums, batching and snapshot-based sync are unexercised.
